dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Emma, how do Canadians greet people?
dialogue.reading: ˈɛmə, ˈhaʊ duː kəˈneɪdiənz ˈɡriːt ˈpiːpəl?

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: We usually shake hands when we meet someone new, whereas Thais wai.
dialogue.reading: wiː ˈjuːʒuəli ˈʃeɪk ˈhændz wɛn wiː ˈmiːt ˈsʌmwʌn ˈnuː, ˌwɛrˈæz ˈtaɪz ˈwaɪ.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Yes, we often hug friends and family, while Thais don't usually hug in public.
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs, wiː ˈɔːfən ˈhʌɡ ˈfrɛndz ənd ˈfæməli, waɪl ˈtaɪz ˈdoʊnt ˈjuːʒuəli ˈhʌɡ ɪn ˈpʌblɪk.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: That's right. My parents don't hug me in front of other people.
dialogue.reading: ðæts ˈraɪt. maɪ ˈpɛrənts ˈdoʊnt ˈhʌɡ miː ɪn ˈfrʌnt əv ˈʌðər ˈpiːpəl.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: And in Quebec, friends often kiss on the face when they meet.
dialogue.reading: ənd ɪn kwɪˈbɛk, ˈfrɛndz ˈɔːfən ˈkɪs ɑːn ðə ˈfeɪs wɛn ðeɪ ˈmiːt.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Really? Thais would feel very embarrassed!
dialogue.reading: ˈriːli? ˈtaɪz wʊd ˈfiːl ˈvɛri ɪmˈbærəst!

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: What about eye contact? In Canada, it's polite to look people in the eye.
dialogue.reading: ˈwʌt əˈbaʊt ˈaɪ ˌkɑːntækt? ɪn ˈkænədə, ɪts pəˈlaɪt tə ˈlʊk ˈpiːpəl ɪn ði ˈaɪ.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: In Thailand, young people often look down when they talk to older people, whereas Canadians look straight at them.
dialogue.reading: ɪn ˈtaɪlænd, ˈjʌŋ ˈpiːpəl ˈɔːfən ˈlʊk ˈdaʊn wɛn ðeɪ ˈtɔːk tu ˈoʊldər ˈpiːpəl, ˌwɛrˈæz kəˈneɪdiənz ˈlʊk ˈstreɪt ət ðɛm.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: So a Thai student who doesn't make eye contact is just being polite?
dialogue.reading: soʊ ə ˈtaɪ ˈstuːdənt huː ˈdʌzənt ˈmeɪk ˈaɪ ˌkɑːntækt ɪz ˈdʒʌst ˈbiːɪŋ pəˈlaɪt?
